pages.text: Notebook, chemistry, day one. A bond is not a stick between balls. Two atoms share an electron because the shared $(thing)wavefunction$() spread over both has lower energy than either alone - the same quantum mechanics as everything else in this book.
The $(item)Chemical Reactor$() is where it starts: $(fluid)Supercritical Solvent$() (gas-dense, liquid-thin) and $(item)Zeolite Catalysts$(), whose pores let only the right molecules meet.
Next: $(item)Molecular Orbital Lattices$() - the bond itself, frozen - and $(item)Chiral Crystals$(), molecules that come in a left hand and a right hand. Life, I will find, only ever uses one.
A crystal full of molecule-sized pores; reactions that fit inside go faster.$(br2)Made in $(item)Catalyst Formulator$().
Electron wavefunctions shared between atoms, frozen into a grid. This is what a chemical bond is.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Left-handed or right-handed, never both. Life only uses one hand.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
